title: Rep urges communities to work together | Borneo Post Online

KAPIT: The communities here need to work together to ensure that the requests they put forward to the government are fulfilled. This call came from Bukit Goram assemblyman Jefferson Jamit Unyat when officiating at the 11th anniversary celebration of Kapit CheQuan Khor Moral Uplifting Society at Meligai Hotel on Saturday evening. “No one including elected people’s representatives can work alone. Therefore, I appeal to all of you to continue to work closely together and with me so that your requests will be fulfilled by the government,” he said. Like elsewhere, Jamit said he was aware of the pressing needs in the constituency that ought to be addressed by the government. As their assemblyman, he said it is his responsibility and duty to work for the constituents to bring more development and improved infrastructure and amenities to them. “In my speech during the recent DUN sitting, I raised some of the pressing issues in Bukit Goram that needed to be addressed. Among them are healthcare services that need to be improved, the setting up of EPF (Employees Provident Fund) office and the overall master plan for the drainage system in and around Kapit. I’m very much aware each time after a heavy downpour, our roads were inundated by flash flood that greatly affected traffic flow,” he elaborated. On another matter, he welcomed members of CheQuan Khor Moral Uplifting Society from Sri Aman, Sarikei, Sibu, Bintulu, Miri, Brunei, Sabah and Kuala Lumpur to Kapit. “I welcome you all to Kapit. Kapit has a lot to offer as an eco-tourism destination like longhouses, handicraft and jungle produce at Terasang Market. Spend two or three days here to explore Kapit’s beauty”, he said. At the same time, Jamit lauded CheQuan Khor Moral Uplifting Society for attracting members from all walks of life. He praised the society for promoting religious harmony, cultural understanding and cooperation as well as encouraging people to practise good moral values and doing charity work for the needy and destitute. He added that their deeds went in line with the government’s effort to promote a caring society. Society chairman Yii Kau Chai informed that the highlight of the two-day celebration from Friday to Saturday was to offer prayers and promote fellowship among the members. The celebration was also to present food package to ten needy and hardcore urban poor as well as study incentives to members’ children who excelled in last year’s school and public examinations. Deputy president of CheQuan Khor Moral Uplifting Society Malaysia, Lee Kee Sen from Kuala Lumpur, and its Sarawak chairman Chia Su Jin joined community leaders and about 200 people at the dinner. At the function, Jamit announced a grant of RM10,000 for the society. Share.
